article_title: Considerations for Supporting a Successful Start to the 2020-2021 School Year for Students with Disabilities
citation: Considerations for supporting a successful start to the 2020-2021 school year for students with disabilities. (2020). National Center for Systemic Improvement (NCSI), WestEd. https://ncsi.wested.org
title: Multi-Tier Systems of Support (MTSS) as a seminal structure for launching the school year supporting quality learning for all students
description: The guidance positions Multi-Tier Systems of Support as an organizing framework through which SEAs can support districts in launching the 2020-2021 school year. It states that "Multi-Tier Systems of Support (MTSS) can provide a seminal structure for launching 2020-2021 in ways that support quality learning for all students." SEA guiding questions cover sustaining and growing district implementation, guidance on data collection, instructional planning including intensive interventions, progress monitoring, and integrated systems attending to both academic and behavioral/social emotional data.
requirements: Sustained or grown district and school implementation of MTSS, with SEA guidance on data collection, instructional planning, and progress monitoring
constraints: The framework is offered for the specific context of launching the 2020-2021 school year under varied reopening conditions
target_learners: all students, including students with disabilities, across tiered supports
target_learning_goals: quality learning supported through integrated academic and behavioral/social emotional systems
examples: The document asks whether the SEA provides guidance for integrated systems of support that attend to both academic and behavioral/social emotional data and planning.
key_sources: Considerations for supporting a successful start to the 2020-2021 school year for students with disabilities. (2020). National Center for Systemic Improvement (NCSI), WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED609257

article_title: How Does Texas Support Students' Social, Emotional, and Academic Development (SEAD)?
citation: The Education Trust. (2023). How Does Texas Support Students' Social, Emotional, and Academic Development (SEAD)?. https://EdTrust.org
title: Multi-tiered or integrated systems of support (MTSS) as wraparound services framework
description: The brief describes MTSS, "also known as wraparound services," as frameworks districts and schools can use to connect services to students, providing access to resources to overcome academic and non-academic barriers to success. When schools identify and provide targeted supports, meet students' health and well-being, and ensure students feel they belong, students can better engage in schools. The brief recommends districts conduct student-level and system-level strengths and needs assessments and measure fidelity of implementation.
requirements: Districts monitor effectiveness of MTSS and conduct strengths and needs assessments
Funding and guidance for evidence-based multi-tiered systems of support
target_learners: K-12 students needing targeted social-emotional, physical and mental health, or family supports, including students experiencing homelessness
target_learning_goals: Removing academic and non-academic barriers so students can engage in school
examples: Texas includes a Children's Commission coordinating interagency services and provides health, housing, and oral health supports and homelessness guidance
key_sources: The Education Trust. (2023). How Does Texas Support Students' Social, Emotional, and Academic Development (SEAD)?. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED628037

article_title: How Does Massachusetts Support Students' Social, Emotional, and Academic Development (SEAD)?
citation: The Education Trust. (2023). How Does Massachusetts Support Students' Social, Emotional, and Academic Development (SEAD)?. EdTrust.org. https://edtrust.org
title: Multi-tiered or integrated systems of support (MTSS) as wraparound services framework
description: The brief describes MTSS, also known as wraparound services, as 'frameworks that districts and schools can use to connect services to students,' providing access to resources to overcome academic and non-academic barriers to success. When schools identify and provide targeted supports, meet students' health and well-being, and ensure students feel they belong, students can better engage in school. Massachusetts supports MTSS through guidance, funding, and Medicaid billing authorization without IEP or IFSP documentation.
requirements: System-level needs assessments by districts and schools; the brief recommends student-level needs and strengths assessments and fidelity-of-implementation monitoring for continuous improvement
constraints: The brief notes Massachusetts should still create an interagency coordination council advancing race equity, expand school counseling to no greater than the 250:1 ratio recommended by the American School Counselor Association, and require participation in the National School Lunch and School Breakfast Programs
target_learners: P-12 students with academic, social-emotional, physical and mental health, and family support needs, prioritized for students with the highest needs
target_learning_goals: Overcoming academic and non-academic barriers so students can better engage in school
examples: Massachusetts expressly authorizes districts to bill Medicaid for services delivered to all Medicaid-enrolled students without requiring IEP or IFSP documentation, prohibits lunch-shaming, and maintains a comprehensive anti-bullying policy naming groups most likely to be bullied
key_sources: The Education Trust. (2023). How Does Massachusetts Support Students' Social, Emotional, and Academic Development (SEAD)?. EdTrust.org. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED630071

article_title: How Does Washington Support Students' Social, Emotional, and Academic Development (SEAD)?
citation: How Does Washington Support Students' Social, Emotional, and Academic Development (SEAD)?. (2023). The Education Trust. https://EdTrust.org
title: Multi-tiered or integrated systems of support (MTSS) as wraparound services
description: The brief describes multi-tiered or integrated systems of support (MTSS), "ALSO KNOWN AS WRAPAROUND SERVICES," as frameworks districts and schools can use to connect services to students, providing "STUDENTS WITH ACCESS TO RESOURCES TO OVERCOME ACADEMIC AND NON-ACADEMIC BARRIERS TO SUCCESS." When schools identify and provide targeted supports, meet students' health and well-being, and foster belonging, students can better engage in school. Washington supports MTSS adoption with guidance and funding, health and housing supports, an anti-bullying policy naming targeted groups, transgender-inclusive athletics and facilities policies, and requirements that districts monitor MTSS progress using student data.
requirements: Districts must conduct student-level and school-level needs and strengths assessments, and monitor the progress and impacts of support systems for continuous improvement
constraints: Washington does not explicitly prioritize multi-tiered systems for students with the highest needs, does not require fidelity-of-implementation reporting, and lacks mandated school counseling at the 250:1 ratio recommended by the American School Counselor Association
target_learners: P-12 students needing targeted social-emotional, physical and mental health, or family supports, including students experiencing homelessness
target_learning_goals: Overcoming academic and non-academic barriers to success; student engagement and sense of belonging in school
examples: Washington prohibits lunch-shaming for unpaid meal debt and provides oral health supports and information for supporting students experiencing homelessness
key_sources: How Does Washington Support Students' Social, Emotional, and Academic Development (SEAD)?. (2023). The Education Trust. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED630072

article_title: Students Experiencing Homelessness: The Conditions and Outcomes of Homelessness among California Students
citation: Burns, D., Espinoza, D., Ondrasek, N., & Yang, M. (2021). Students experiencing homelessness: The conditions and outcomes of homelessness among California students. Learning Policy Institute. https://learningpolicyinstitute.org/product/students-experiencing-homelessness
title: Multi-tiered systems of support (MTSS) as a school-level structure for supporting students experiencing homelessness
description: MTSS is described as a school-level coordinative structure that integrates academic, behavioral, and social-emotional supports in tiers. The report states that "School-level structures like multi-tiered systems of support (MTSS) can support students experiencing homelessness by providing an intervention framework that integrates academic, behavioral, and social and emotional competencies." It recommends districts implement MTSS so services reach students who need them without cumbersome procedures, and notes MTSS can be tailored to individual students' specific needs, which matters given this group's complex needs.
requirements: Well implementation to provide services effectively, which the report notes can be made challenging by the highly mobile nature of homelessness
constraints: Implementation is challenged by the highly mobile nature of homelessness, as the article states
target_learners: K–12 students experiencing homelessness
target_learning_goals: Integrated academic, behavioral, and social and emotional competencies
examples: The report recommends districts implement school-level coordinative structures such as MTSS to efficiently identify and meet student needs, alongside community school wraparound supports
key_sources: Burns, D., Espinoza, D., Ondrasek, N., & Yang, M. (2021). Students experiencing homelessness: The conditions and outcomes of homelessness among California students. Learning Policy Institute. https://learningpolicyinstitute.org/product/students-experiencing-homelessness

article_title: Reconciling Contemporary Approaches to School Attendance and School Absenteeism: Toward Promotion and Nimble Response, Global Policy Review and Implementation, and Future Adaptability (Part 1)
citation: Kearney CA, Gonzálvez C, Graczyk PA and Fornander MJ (2019) Reconciling Contemporary Approaches to School Attendance and School Absenteeism: Toward Promotion and Nimble Response, Global Policy Review and Implementation, and Future Adaptability (Part 1). Front. Psychol. 10:2222. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02222
title: Multi-tiered system of supports (MTSS) model for school attendance and absenteeism
description: The review describes an MTSS model arranging SA/A prevention and intervention into three tiers: Tier 1 universal approaches promoting school-wide attendance and preventing absenteeism for all students; Tier 2 approaches for emerging, acute, or mild to moderate absenteeism; and Tier 3 approaches for chronic and severe absenteeism. The model's dimensions include severity of absenteeism, degree of risk or contextual factors, target of intervention, and intervention intensity, designed to eschew a "wait to fail" mentality in favor of active monitoring and immediate intervention.
requirements: Implementation fidelity; attendance measures included in district MTSS models
constraints: Remains in development; absenteeism rates in some schools are so overwhelming that entry into Tiers 2 and 3 is strained; how it fits with academic, behavioral, and social MTSS approaches remains to be seen
target_learners: all students in a school, with targeted subgroups at Tiers 2 and 3
target_learning_goals: promoting school attendance, preventing and remediating absenteeism and dropout
examples: Cook et al. (2017) evaluated a program with Tier 1 home visits and mobile telephone contact, Tier 2 attendance data monitoring, and Tier 3 referrals to specialists for chronic absenteeism
key_sources: Kearney CA, Gonzálvez C, Graczyk PA and Fornander MJ (2019) Reconciling Contemporary Approaches to School Attendance and School Absenteeism: Toward Promotion and Nimble Response, Global Policy Review and Implementation, and Future Adaptability (Part 1). Front. Psychol. 10:2222. https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02222

article_title: Inclusive pedagogy in practice within the multi-tiered systems of support framework: a design-based research in a Chinese EFL classroom
citation: Lin, T., Mullick, J., & Campbell, M. (2026). Inclusive pedagogy in practice within the multi-tiered systems of support framework: a design-based research in a Chinese EFL classroom. Instructional Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-025-09754-3
title: Multi-Tiered System of Support (MTSS) framework with three tiers of support
description: MTSS is described as "an evidence-based framework designed to enhance academic achievement, behaviour, and social-emotional well-being through tiered levels of support". It comprises three tiers — Tier 1 universal, Tier 2 targeted, and Tier 3 intensive — and two key dimensions, Response to Intervention and Positive Behavioural Interventions and Supports. In this study MTSS guided both content teaching and classroom management in a Chinese EFL classroom, combined with TPRS to deliver inclusive pedagogy.
requirements: Tier 1 universal instruction establishing academic skills, prosocial behaviour, and emotional well-being for all students, with Tier 2 targeted and Tier 3 intensive support layered on for students needing more
constraints: The article notes MTSS's adaptation in culturally diverse contexts such as China remains underexplored, and behavioural support may be perceived as secondary to academic rigour in exam-driven systems
target_learners: elementary EFL students across low-, mid-, and high-performance levels, including students with SEN and neurodiverse conditions
target_learning_goals: English language proficiency
engagement and on-task behaviour
social-emotional well-being
examples: The first author applied MTSS as sole teacher of one class for three years, offering EFL lessons three times per week in Grade 1, four times in Grade 2, and daily in Grade 3
key_sources: Lin, T., Mullick, J., & Campbell, M. (2026). Inclusive pedagogy in practice within the multi-tiered systems of support framework: a design-based research in a Chinese EFL classroom. Instructional Science. https://doi.org/10.1007/s11251-025-09754-3

article_title: Teachers “finding peace in a frantic world”: An experimental study of self-taught and instructor-led mindfulness program formats on acceptability, effectiveness, and mechanisms.
citation: Montero-Marin et al. (2021). Teachers “Finding Peace in a Frantic World”: An Experimental Study of Self-Taught and Instructor-Led Mindfulness Program Formats on Acceptability, Effectiveness, and Mechanisms. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000542
title: Mindfulness and self-compassion skills as psychological mechanisms linking mindfulness training implementation to teacher occupational well-being
description: The article draws on a comprehensive theoretical framework in which adequate implementation of mindfulness training enables teachers to develop the skills of mindfulness and self-compassion, which, applied in daily life through practice, lead to improved occupational health and well-being. Mindfulness skills help teachers "recognize their distress without judgment, be open to it, and learn to self-soothe," while self-compassion skills increase the ability to regulate intense negative emotions in response to stressors. This framework motivated the study's mediation analyses and the hypothesis that the two delivery formats might produce different patterns of skill acquisition and mediation.
requirements: An adequate implementation of mindfulness training so that skills are developed and applied in daily life through practice
constraints: The framework's causal links between skills and outcomes were tested via mediation analysis without a no-intervention arm in this study
target_learners: secondary school teachers
target_learning_goals: managing occupational stress and improving well-being through mindfulness and self-compassion skills
examples: The trial tested whether mindfulness and self-compassion gains mediated improvements in well-being, stress, anxiety, depression, and burnout in each delivery format
key_sources: Montero-Marin et al. (2021). Teachers “Finding Peace in a Frantic World”: An Experimental Study of Self-Taught and Instructor-Led Mindfulness Program Formats on Acceptability, Effectiveness, and Mechanisms. Journal of Educational Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/edu0000542

article_title: Moving-Target Intelligent Tutoring System for Marksmanship Training
citation: Vladimir Zotov & Eric Kramkowski. (2023). Moving-Target Intelligent Tutoring System for Marksmanship Training. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-022-00308-z
title: MT-ITS: embedded moving-target marksmanship tutoring system
description: MT-ITS is a software-based tutor embedded into the digital sight of an instrumented rifle, operating in the Virtual Immersive Soldier Simulator. Its two feedback mechanisms are "a real-time correction of aiming" delivered by the Smart Sight System, which presents the optimal point of aim as a red rectangle on the target, and an after-action feedback showing each shot sequentially plus a statistical summary. It incorporates domain, tutor, and user-interface components of a standard ITS; its learner model is largely undeveloped, and the system is tuned for novice shooters.
requirements: Requires the VBS2 simulation environment and instrumented rifle tracking to compute and deliver point-of-aim cues and record shot data
constraints: Limited by poverty of sensor inputs, restrictions of the simulation environment, and deficiencies of instrumentation, placing it in a category of an advanced feedback training system with some AI elements rather than a fully-fledged ITS
Applicability was limited to novice shooters because the learner model is not well-elaborated
target_learners: novice shooters from Reserve Canadian Army units with little to no firearms experience
target_learning_goals: engaging moving targets: estimating distance and speed, adjusting point of aim, analyzing missed shots, and learning tracking techniques
examples: In the experiment, MT-ITS trainees alternated cued and non-cued trials and received after-action feedback with per-shot diagrams and a summary slide; in the second training block the target dropped after three hits to emphasize engagement speed.
key_sources: Vladimir Zotov & Eric Kramkowski. (2023). Moving-Target Intelligent Tutoring System for Marksmanship Training. International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education. https://doi.org/10.1007/s40593-022-00308-z

article_title: Effects of Mathematics Integration in a Teaching Methods Course on Self-Efficacy of Preservice Agricultural Education Teachers
citation: Christopher T. Stripling and T. Grady Roberts. (2013). Effects of Mathematics Integration in a Teaching Methods Course on Self-Efficacy of Preservice Agricultural Education Teachers. Journal of Agricultural Education, 54(2), 114-129. https://doi.org/10.5032/jae.2013.02114
title: Mathematics teaching and integration strategies (MTIS) treatment in the agricultural teaching methods course
description: The MTIS treatment was incorporated into the teaching methods course at the University of Florida and, beyond the course's normal requirements, "added the following three elements: (a) a lecture on the seven components of a math-enhanced lesson , (b) random assignment of the NCTM sub -standards among the preservice teachers, and (c) requiring two of the micro-teaching lessons to be math-enhanced." Treatment-group teachers delivered math-enhanced lessons to peers using the National Research Center for Career and Technical Education's seven components, observing up to 12 peer math-enhanced lessons while roleplaying as secondary students.
requirements: Requires the teaching methods course structure of lectures and peer micro-teachings, NCTM sub-standards cross-referenced to National Agriculture, Food and Natural Resources Career Cluster Content Standards, and the seven components of a math-enhanced lesson model.
constraints: The article reports the treatment did not significantly change any of the three measured efficacy constructs, and the experimental group generally had slightly lower self-efficacy scores after the treatment.
target_learners: preservice agricultural education teachers in their final year of a teacher education program
target_learning_goals: teaching contextualized mathematics within agricultural education curricula
examples: Each treatment participant received a lecture on the seven components of a math-enhanced lesson, was randomly assigned two of the 13 NCTM sub-standards, and integrated mathematics into two of the eight normally required micro-teachings.
key_sources: Christopher T. Stripling and T. Grady Roberts. (2013). Effects of Mathematics Integration in a Teaching Methods Course on Self-Efficacy of Preservice Agricultural Education Teachers. Journal of Agricultural Education, 54(2), 114-129. https://doi.org/10.5032/jae.2013.02114

article_title: The Effect of Metacognitive Teaching and Mathematical Prior Knowledge on Mathematical Logical Thinking Ability and Self-Regulated Learning
citation: Aminah, M., Kusumah, Y. S., Suryadi, D., & Sumarmo, U. (2018). The Effect of Metacognitive Teaching and Mathematical Prior Knowledge on Mathematical Logical Thinking Ability and Self-Regulated Learning. International Journal of Instruction, 11(3), 45-62. https://doi.org/10.12973/iji.2018.1134a
title: Metacognitive teaching-learning approach (MTLA) with four components: think-aloud, metacognitive scaffolding, discussions, and metacognitive journal writing
description: MTLA is a teaching approach that emphasizes promoting students' awareness of their abilities by accustoming them to pose metacognitive questions covering understanding of concepts and problems, connecting new knowledge with previous knowledge, using relevant strategies, and reflecting on process and outcome. In this research it comprised think-aloud modeling by the teacher, metacognitive scaffolding through questioning (linked to Vygotsky's ZPD), pair, group and class discussion grounded in social constructivism, and metacognitive journal writing requiring students to clarify and reflect on their thought. It was implemented over one full semester against conventional teaching.
requirements: Requires teachers to model thinking aloud and to pose scaffolding questions that bridge what students can do alone and with assistance
Requires social interaction structures (pair, group, class discussion) and journal-writing tasks that prompt metacognitive reflection
constraints: In this study it was applied to tenth-grade mathematics content (exponents and logarithms, quadratic functions, quadratic equations and inequalities, linear equation systems) in an Indonesian senior high school
target_learners: tenth-grade senior high school mathematics students
target_learning_goals: mathematical logical thinking ability
self-regulated learning
examples: The experimental class received MTL across four mathematics topics for one full semester while the control class received conventional teaching
key_sources: Aminah, M., Kusumah, Y. S., Suryadi, D., & Sumarmo, U. (2018). The Effect of Metacognitive Teaching and Mathematical Prior Knowledge on Mathematical Logical Thinking Ability and Self-Regulated Learning. International Journal of Instruction, 11(3), 45-62. https://doi.org/10.12973/iji.2018.1134a

article_title: Effects of Mathematics Integration in a Teaching Methods Course on Mathematics Ability of Preservice Agricultural Education Teachers
citation: Christopher T. Stripling and T. Grady Roberts. (2014). Effects of Mathematics Integration in a Teaching Methods Course on Mathematics Ability of Preservice Agricultural Education Teachers. Journal of Agricultural Education, 55(3), 1-16. https://doi.org/10.5032/jae.2014.03001
title: MTIS treatment: three added elements in the teaching methods course
description: The mathematics teaching and integration strategies (MTIS) treatment was incorporated into the lab sections of an agricultural teaching methods course. Beyond the normal course requirements, "the treatment added the following three elements: (a) a lecture on the seven components of a math -enhanced lesson, (b) random assignment of the NCTM sub -standards among the preservice teachers, and (c) requiring two of the micro-teaching lessons to be math-enhanced". Treatment-group members taught two NCTM sub-standards to peers and observed peers teaching up to 12 math-enhanced lessons while role-playing as secondary students.
requirements: The treatment was delivered within the existing teaching methods course structure of lectures and labs with eight normally required micro-teachings
The lecture on the seven components was reviewed by an expert to ensure validity
constraints: Random assignment of subjects was not possible; the MTIS treatment was randomly assigned to two of three self-registered course sections
target_learners: senior preservice agricultural education teachers
target_learning_goals: mathematics ability
teaching contextualized mathematics in agriculture
examples: Each treatment participant participated in the math-enhanced lesson lecture, integrated mathematics into two of the eight normally required micro-teachings, and observed peers teaching up to 12 math-enhanced lessons

article_title: "MyTeachingPartner--Math/Science" Pre-Kindergarten Curricula and Teacher Supports: Associations with Children's Mathematics and Science Learning
citation: Kinzie, M. B., Vick Whittaker, J., Williford, A. P., DeCoster, J., McGuire, P., Lee, Y., & Kilday, C. R. (2014). MyTeachingPartner-Math/Science pre-kindergarten curricula and teacher supports: Associations with children's mathematics and science learning. Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 29, 586-599. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2014.06.007
title: MTP-M/S instructional design model: structured inquiry balanced with teacher-guided teaching, anchored in situated cognition and a modified 5E cycle
description: The article articulates a design model for early mathematics and science activities that draws on "instructional theories related to structured inquiry, situated cognition anchored in authentic investigation, and cognitive development." Structured inquiry is placed mid-way on a continuum from teacher-directed to student-driven: "teachers ensure exposure to key constructs by posing questions, suggesting procedures, and guiding students learning" while children investigate with materials and observe phenomena. Activities begin with authentic everyday problems (e.g., fairly sharing cookies) and conclude with students analyzing, discussing, extending and applying what they learned, described as "a modiﬁcation of the 5E Model".
requirements: Activities must balance meaningful student-centered interactions with teacher-guided intentional teaching that ensures exposure to key skills and concepts, as the article recommends citing Justice and Pullen (2003).
constraints: The model was designed for pre-kindergarten mathematics and science activities of 15-20 minutes in whole- or small-group format.
target_learners: pre-kindergarten children (average age 4.76 years) in state-funded full-day classrooms
target_learning_goals: early mathematics (number sense, operations, geometry, measurement)
early science (life, earth, and physical science concepts and inquiry skills)
examples: Children follow life cycles of plants, animals, and themselves across the year; with seedlings they have planted, they predict and observe outcomes under light and water, light but no water, water but no light, and neither.
Inquiries are often launched through children's literature, with 18 books in mathematics and 28 in science.
key_sources: Kinzie, M. B., Vick Whittaker, J., Williford, A. P., DeCoster, J., McGuire, P., Lee, Y., & Kilday, C. R. (2014). MyTeachingPartner-Math/Science pre-kindergarten curricula and teacher supports: Associations with children's mathematics and science learning. Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 29, 586-599. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2014.06.007

article_title: "MyTeachingPartner--Math/Science" Pre-Kindergarten Curricula and Teacher Supports: Associations with Children's Mathematics and Science Learning
citation: Kinzie, M. B., Vick Whittaker, J., Williford, A. P., DeCoster, J., McGuire, P., Lee, Y., & Kilday, C. R. (2014). MyTeachingPartner-Math/Science pre-kindergarten curricula and teacher supports: Associations with children's mathematics and science learning. Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 29, 586-599. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2014.06.007
title: MyTeachingPartner-Math/Science (MTP-M/S) curricula: 66 activities per domain across 33 weeks
description: MTP-M/S is a pair of year-long pre-kindergarten curricula, one in mathematics and one in science, each with 66 activities presented in an explicit four-step inquiry format. "Each curriculum includes two activities (each activity 15–20 min in length) every week, for 33 weeks across the school year", plus weekly center-time options for revisiting activities with small groups of purposefully selected students. MTP-Math prioritizes number sense, with "over one-half of MTP-Math activities" in that domain, and covers operations, geometry, and measurement; MTP-Science addresses life, earth, and physical science with activities to "predict, observe, analyze, and describe" findings using simple tools such as a hand lens and balance.
requirements: Teachers receive within-activity supports including language to model and elicit, questioning recommendations, adaptations for differentiation, and suggested extension activities.
constraints: The curricula were designed to stand alone but reference concepts reflective of both mathematics and science wherever possible.
target_learners: pre-kindergarten children in Title 1, state-funded classrooms
target_learning_goals: early mathematics knowledge and skills
early science knowledge and inquiry skills
examples: Mathematics activities use a number chart with color-coded numerals and ten-frames (blue for tens, orange for ones) to illustrate numbers 0 to 39, reinforcing early place value conceptions.
key_sources: Kinzie, M. B., Vick Whittaker, J., Williford, A. P., DeCoster, J., McGuire, P., Lee, Y., & Kilday, C. R. (2014). MyTeachingPartner-Math/Science pre-kindergarten curricula and teacher supports: Associations with children's mathematics and science learning. Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 29, 586-599. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2014.06.007

article_title: "MyTeachingPartner--Math/Science" Pre-Kindergarten Curricula and Teacher Supports: Associations with Children's Mathematics and Science Learning
citation: Kinzie, M. B., Vick Whittaker, J., Williford, A. P., DeCoster, J., McGuire, P., Lee, Y., & Kilday, C. R. (2014). MyTeachingPartner-Math/Science pre-kindergarten curricula and teacher supports: Associations with children's mathematics and science learning. Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 29, 586-599. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2014.06.007
title: MTP-M/S Plus hybrid teacher support system: online demonstration videos, weekly challenges, and spaced workshops
description: The Plus package supplements the MTP-M/S curricula with a hybrid professional development system combining online supports with in-person workshops (one full-day summer workshop and seven 2.5-hour workshops, about 23.5 hours total outside the classroom). Online, the authors "provided over 130, 2–3 min demonstration videos that illustrated high-quality teacher–child interactions" — one or more per activity — plus weekly 5-minute video-based teaching challenges with expert feedback, a monthly quality-teaching dimension video, brief teaching tips of 25 words or fewer, and a library of 150 video examples. Supports are anchored in teachers' authentic tasks and use the Classroom Assessment Scoring System (CLASS) framework for quality interactions.
requirements: Workshops were designed to encourage teachers' use of the online support system and to provide reflection and peer discussion on teaching practice.
constraints: The hybrid format aimed to minimize professional development time required, compared to the average of 49 hours found effective in the review the article cites (Yoon et al., 2007).
target_learners: pre-kindergarten teachers, including those without strong mathematics/science preparation or experience
target_learning_goals: curricular implementation fidelity (adherence and quality)
teachers' pedagogical and content knowledge in mathematics and science
examples: Plus teachers attended an average of 6.18 workshops (SD = 1.17) and spent an average of 10.52 hours (SD = 6.80) on the support website, with usage ranging from 1.18 to 21.05 hours.
key_sources: Kinzie, M. B., Vick Whittaker, J., Williford, A. P., DeCoster, J., McGuire, P., Lee, Y., & Kilday, C. R. (2014). MyTeachingPartner-Math/Science pre-kindergarten curricula and teacher supports: Associations with children's mathematics and science learning. Early Childhood Research Quarterly, 29, 586-599. http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.ecresq.2014.06.007

article_title: Racing against the Vocabulary Gap: Matthew Effects in Early Vocabulary Instruction and Intervention
citation: Coyne, M. D., McCoach, D. B., Ware, S., Austin, C. R., Loftus-Rattan, S. M., & Baker, D. L. (2019). Racing Against the Vocabulary Gap: Matthew Effects in Early Vocabulary Instruction and Intervention. Exceptional Children, 85(2), 163–179. https://doi.org/10.1177/0014402918789162
title: Supplement Tier-1 classroom vocabulary instruction with small-group Tier-2 intervention for students identified as at risk through universal screening
description: The article supports providing targeted small-group supplemental vocabulary intervention within an MTSS framework for kindergarten students screened as at risk. By "identifying students who were at greatest risk for not responding to classroom vocabulary instruction," the team was able to "lessen Matthew effects for these students on experimenter-developed measures of target word learning and listening comprehension." The intervention reteached and reinforced Tier-1 vocabulary through engaging activities with immediate corrective feedback.
requirements: Universal screening at the beginning of the year to identify students at risk for not responding to Tier-1 instruction
Small groups of three or four students with trained interventionists
Alignment between Tier-2 intervention and Tier-1 classroom vocabulary lessons
constraints: Required approximately double the instructional time compared to Tier-1 only
Did not impact standardized measures of overall vocabulary knowledge
Not intensive enough to close the listening comprehension gap for students with the lowest initial vocabulary knowledge
target_learners: kindergarten students at risk for language and learning difficulties
target_learning_goals: target word learning
listening comprehension of passages containing taught vocabulary
examples: Kindergarten teachers provided 20 min of whole-group direct vocabulary instruction per day over 22 weeks; half of at-risk students were randomly assigned to receive 30 min per day, 4 days per week of small-group Tier-2 intervention
key_sources: Coyne, M. D., McCoach, D. B., Ware, S., Austin, C. R., Loftus-Rattan, S. M., & Baker, D. L. (2019). Racing Against the Vocabulary Gap: Matthew Effects in Early Vocabulary Instruction and Intervention. Exceptional Children, 85(2), 163–179. https://doi.org/10.1177/0014402918789162

title: MyTeachingPartner-Secondary (MTP-S) video-based teacher coaching intervention
description: MTP-S is a year-long professional development coaching program for secondary teachers that "uses the Classroom Assessment Scoring System-Secondary (CLASS-S) as a framework for guiding video-based interactions between teachers and a highly trained coach." Teachers videotape their focal class, coaches select brief segments tied to CLASS-S dimensions, teachers reflect online, and each cycle ends with a 20–30 minute phone conference, repeated approximately every 6 weeks.
requirements: Teachers record typical sessions of a selected focal course and complete coaching cycles with an assigned master-teacher coach throughout the academic year
constraints: The article notes few programs have been empirically shown to improve student achievement, positioning MTP-S among a small set of validated options
target_learners: secondary school students (middle and high school)
target_learning_goals: developmentally sensitive teacher–student interactions
classroom organization and instructional support
examples: In the trial, 86 teachers were randomly assigned to MTP-S or regular in-service training within five schools, and both groups attended a 3-hour pre-year workshop

title: MyTeachingPartner (MTP) video-based coaching program for 4Rs implementation
description: MTP is a standardized, video-based coaching program supporting teachers using the 4Rs curriculum. Every two weeks teachers videotape their instruction; the coach edits the tape into short segments focused on a specific CLASS dimension of interaction, posts them with written "prompts" to a private website, and then meets the teacher for an in-person 30-minute conference to problem-solve and plan future lessons. Teachers complete 8 coaching cycles per year.
requirements: Teachers videotape their implementation of instructional activities every two weeks and send footage to their coach
Coaches complete 8 MTP coaching cycles with each teacher across the academic year
target_learners: Grade 3-5 teachers in New York City public elementary schools
target_learning_goals: Improve fidelity of implementation of the 4Rs social-emotional and literacy curriculum
Improve quality of teacher-student interactions as defined by the CLASS framework

article_title: Enhancing Team Strategies and Tools to Enhance Performance and Patient Safety Performance Through Medical Movies, Massive Open Online Courses, and 3D Virtual Simulation-Based Interprofessional Education: Mixed Methods Double-Blind Quasi-Experimental Study.
citation: Khuansiri Narajeenron et al. (2025). Enhancing Team Strategies and Tools to Enhance Performance and Patient Safety Performance Through Medical Movies, Massive Open Online Courses, and 3D Virtual Simulation–Based Interprofessional Education: Mixed Methods Double-Blind Quasi-Experimental Study. Journal of Medical Internet Research. https://doi.org/10.2196/67001
title: Modified TeamSTEPPS Team Performance Observation Tool (mTPOT) with a priori profession-specific behavioral anchors
description: A validated modification of the Team Performance Observation Tool for assessing team performance in 3D computer-based or VR SimBIE, covering the five TeamSTEPPS domains. "For each item in the TPOT, behavioral anchors were defined a priori," with separate anchors per profession tied to scenario events (e.g., check-back verification of patient name, drug name, dose, route, rate, and critical K level). Content validation by 3 experts achieved scale-level content validity index scores >0.8; 12 blinded interprofessional raters reviewed 174 video clips.
requirements: Rater training: 10-minute rater error training, 40-minute performance dimension training, and 60-minute frame-of-reference group discussion
Blinded video review with obscured date/time sensor data and study codes held by a single research assistant
constraints: Complete mTPOT data and assessment tools are proprietary and not publicly available
Items were removed for professions lacking a suitable behavioral anchor for the simulation
Weighted κ for the doctor and airway nurse raters was <0.6 in both assessments
target_learners: Clinical undergraduate students across 5 health care professions
target_learning_goals: Measuring interprofessional teamwork behaviors across team structure, communication, leadership, situation monitoring, and mutual support
examples: Overall interrater reliability exceeded 85% agreement, with weighted κ values ranging from 0.49 to 0.98

article_title: Efficacy of modified team-based learning in a flipped classroom for an acute-care nursing course: A mixed-methods study.
citation: Murata, H., Asakawa, S., Kawamura, T., Yamauchi, H., Takahashi, O., & Henker, R. (2023). Efficacy of modified team‐based learning in a flipped classroom for an acute‐care nursing course: A mixed‐methods study. Nursing Open, 10, 4786–4796. https://doi.org/10.1002/nop2.1730
title: M-TBL: modified team-based learning delivered in a digitally powered flipped classroom without peer evaluation
description: M-TBL is "TBL without the peer evaluation step, which is the final step in the original (US) version of TBL". Peer evaluation was removed because Japanese nursing students were reported to be reluctant to engage in it. In the acute-care course, students viewed 30–45 min teacher-made lecture videos on demand one to two weeks before class, took an individual readiness assurance test of about five questions worth 30% of the grade, then worked in randomly allocated groups of five on three paper-based simulated cases, developing a nursing plan and presenting it; three teachers scored the group work with unified rubrics for 20% of the grade.
requirements: Students must view the on-demand lecture videos before class, since IRATs related to the videos ensured students could only participate in the class if they viewed the video
Groups of five, based on reports that groups of five to seven are optimal
constraints: Designed and tested with Japanese undergraduate nursing students in one mandatory acute-care nursing course at a single university
target_learners: Third-year undergraduate nursing students
target_learning_goals: Team approach for inter-professional collaboration
Critical-thinking disposition
Self-directed learning and mastery of practical nursing skills
examples: Three paper-based simulated cases (gastrointestinal, cardiovascular, neurological disease) were sequenced to align with disease/therapeutics and pharmacology content across 15 class meetings
key_sources: Murata, H., Asakawa, S., Kawamura, T., Yamauchi, H., Takahashi, O., & Henker, R. (2023). Efficacy of modified team‐based learning in a flipped classroom for an acute‐care nursing course: A mixed‐methods study. Nursing Open, 10, 4786–4796. https://doi.org/10.1002/nop2.1730
